summary: Research-and-decision dispatch. Recommendation: OPTION B (primitive bot), with the caveat that 'B' overstates the work required -- the argument was already won on the record before #607 merged. Two load-bearing premises in the revised task description are factually wrong and their correction inverts the decision. (1) PR #607 did NOT settle the falsum question: bot-as-atom (instBotProposition [Bot Atom] := <.atom bot>) dates to PR #89, the original definitions commit; #607's diff carries it as unchanged context. #607 renamed impl->imp, swapped per-type scoped infix notation for HasAnd/HasOr/HasImp/HasNot instances, and added a not_eq grind lemma -- it never touched the constructor set. (2) PR #648's blocking review is stale, not adverse: thomaskwaring APPROVED on 2026-07-06 after negotiating a compromise on Zulip (2026-06-28, 'if we are going to have bot as a primitive, we should also have efq') that Benjamin implemented on 2026-06-29; all five of his inline comments were answered 2026-07-13. The lone outstanding CHANGES_REQUESTED is ctchou's from 2026-06-15, whose FIRST bullet reads 'I like the idea of adding \bot as a primitive' and whose four points are all now addressed. A third participant (Matthew Doty) independently backed primitive falsum on DPLL grounds. There is no standing opposition on the record. Also corrected: the 'HasBot gap' is not a blocker -- this fork's own prior research already retracted that recommendation; Mathlib's Bot/Top supply bot/top and the fork already uses them, so a five-primitive Proposition registers against merged #607 with zero new typeclasses. What DID land is a documentation bug: upstream Defs.lean:36-37 promises HasBot/HasTop instances for classes that exist nowhere in upstream. PR #648 recommendation: REWORK AND REBASE, do not close, do not leave pending -- and do NOT widen its scope to the fork's current gated-efq design (that is the deferred fragment work thomaskwaring explicitly agreed to postpone; widening forfeits a standing approval). No .lean file was created, moved, or edited. Nothing was posted to GitHub or Zulip; all gh and Zulip access was read-only.

decisions_made: Recommend Option B (primitive bot) -- reject Option A and Option C.

Reject Option A: premise motivating it does not exist (#607 is orthogonal to falsum); 512/1614 declarations would gain a [Bot Atom] gate; three central semantic definitions (Tautology, IValid, and substitution closure) change MEANING not just signature; risks a 42,166-line zero-sorry development. The one genuine benefit (MValid loses its bot_forces quantifier -- thomaskwaring's argument, correct for minimal logic alone) is outweighed within the same development, since the IPL and CPL layers pay a side-condition tax to buy it.
Reject Option C: forfeits a 42k-line sorry-free development two upstream reviewers signalled they want, blocks #649, and does not even avoid the Connectives/Operators reconciliation work.

PR #648: rework and rebase; keep scope exactly as approved (four files, ungated efq, IPL base, minimal logic deferred); re-request review from ctchou itemising the four dispositions; note thomaskwaring's approval stands.
Do NOT widen #648 to the fork's [IsIntuitionistic T]-gated efq design -- that is the deferred fragment work; it belongs in a follow-up PR.
